items.name: Meta Muse Wonder & Muse Wonder Full
items.summary: Meta's new frontier models launched Oct 12, built for personal and professional agentic work with Active Memory (retains context across conversations) and Active Focus (sustains multi-step tasks, recovers from errors). Muse Wonder ships via the Meta Model API and Muse Code; the stronger Wonder Full is Muse Code subscribers only. Meta claims state-of-the-art coding and finance/legal agent performance.

items.name: Anthropic Claude Haiku 5.5
items.summary: Launched Oct 7, Anthropic's fastest and cheapest small model with 1M-token context and adjustable effort, priced at $0.10/1M input and $0.50/1M output tokens to match OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna — aimed squarely at high-volume agent workloads like classification, extraction, and support.

items.name: Inner Sky Labs physical AI foundation models
items.summary: The Mumbai-based Miko maker unveiled a hardware-agnostic platform of foundation models for robots and physical machines: Drishti (vision), Shruti (audio), Sparsh (touch) perception models plus Kriya/Prana/Karma action models, with Kavach — an independent safety layer that vetoes unsafe moves before execution. A ~₹300 crore funding round is nearing closure.

items.name: Amazon Strands Decider 2B
items.summary: Amazon's 2B-parameter decision model ships Oct 1 as free open weights with training data and scripts — a classifier that returns typed verdicts with probabilities instead of prose, designed to run on local CPU/GPU so teams can keep routing and moderation calls off frontier APIs.

items.name: Mistral Large 4 (preview)
items.summary: Mistral previewed Large 4, a 1-trillion-parameter open model — but early coverage notes it still trails the leading Chinese open models, and Ecosia publicly switched away from Mistral over quality concerns. Still one to watch as Europe's flagship open model.
